introduction.summary: This specification records the project purpose, stakeholder constraints and unresolved decisions stated in the source evidence below.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-001
items.detail: Design a secure email security gateway for a university that protects students, faculty, staff, and administrators from phishing, malicious attachments, spoofed messages, and suspicious links.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-002
items.detail: The system should inspect incoming and outgoing email traffic, detect suspicious messages, quarantine potentially harmful emails, generate security alerts, and allow authorized administrators to review and release quarantined messages.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-003
items.detail: The platform should maintain audit logs of filtering decisions and administrator actions, integrate with the university identity system, and provide a dashboard for monitoring email security events.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-004
items.detail: The solution should be secure, reliable, scalable, and manageable for university-wide deployment.

sdlc.justification: No differentiating input evidence is provided to select among Agile, DevSecOps, Spiral, V-Model, Waterfall, Hybrid, or Incremental models. All candidates receive equal suitability scores of 40 out of 100. The decision remains provisional due to unknown factors including budget, delivery, failure consequences, feedback, legacy, regulation, schedule, stability, uncertainty, verification. Without explicit evidence on these factors, no model can be ranked as superior.
tradeoffs: Recurring delivery requires stakeholder review and backlog refinement; a cycle does not guarantee completeness or remove unresolved decisions.
